VIDEO.title: What Paul Really Means by Righteousness (Romans 4)
VIDEO.series: The Book of Romans, Every Word (playlist of 28 videos)

kicker: Study aid · Romans 4:1-25 · Episode 7 (#7 of 28 in the playlist)
hand: God's promise keeping, our promise trusting
SUMMARY: The teacher reads Romans 4:1-25. Abraham 'believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness' (4:3). To the one who does not work but believes in Him who justifies the ungodly, faith is counted as righteousness, as David also says (4:4-8). Abraham was counted righteous before he was circumcised, so he is the father of all who believe (4:9-12). The promise came through the righteousness of faith, not the Law (4:13-16). Abraham believed God, who gives life to the dead, and it was written for our sake too: Jesus 'was delivered over on account of our transgressions, and was raised on account of our justification' (4:17-25).

Recap: Romans 1:17 explains 1:16. The righteousness of God is revealed out of God's covenant faithfulness into the faithful response of the believer. Romans 4 replays that pattern through Abraham, again and again (4:17, 18, 20, 21, 24, 25).

Abraham came from Ur (Genesis 11) and was counted righteous before circumcision (Genesis 15:6; 17:10-14). That paves the way for Gentiles to be his sons and daughters. In Genesis 15, a deep sleep fell on Abraham and God alone passed between the pieces: the covenant rests entirely on God's faithfulness.

Romans 4:5 is shocking: God 'justifies the ungodly,' yet Exodus 23:7 says 'I will not justify the guilty.' Everyone is wicked (3:10-18) and the Law brings wrath (4:15). God acquits the wicked not by ignoring sin but because the righteousness of Christ is applied to them by faith. Other connections: Psalm 32:1-2; Genesis 12:3; 13:16; 17:5; Isaiah 53:11.

Paul uses 'righteousness' eight times in Romans 4. The teacher suggests reading it as 'covenant belonging' and walks through 4:3, 5, 6, 9, 11, 13 and 22 that way. Paul has rubbed the Old Testament into his words like a dry rub on meat on the grill.

The lesson: 'Righteousness is the covenant bond God forms and believers step into by faith.' Marriage pictures it: God's promise keeping and our promise trusting. The application is a cascading waterfall filling plunge pools: God is the source, and our faith is the open basin that receives and overflows (Psalm 37:4-6; Philippians 3:9).
QUOTES: Righteousness is the covenant bond God forms and believers step into by faith.
According to Paul righteousness is God's promise keeping and our promise trusting.
My faith is not a matching contribution to what God has done or is doing in my life.
God's covenant faithfulness is the waterfall itself, initiating and sustaining and pouring out towards me and towards you.

LSB_QUOTES.text: For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.”
But to the one who does not work, but believes upon Him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted as righteousness,
He who was delivered over on account of our transgressions, and was raised on account of our justification.

left.text: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about—but not before God! For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.”

right.text: And He brought him outside and said, “Now look toward the heavens, and number the stars, if you are able to number them.” And He said to him, “So shall your seed be.” Then he believed in Yahweh; and He counted it to him as righteousness.

lines.text: Boasting was excluded in 3:27; now Paul shows it from the Law's own story. Abraham, the forefather of Israel, had nothing to boast about before God.
The teacher: Paul will bring Genesis 15:6 up again and again in this chapter (4:3, 9, 22).

left.text: Now to the one who works, his wage is not counted according to grace, but according to what is due. But to the one who does not work, but believes upon Him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted as righteousness,

right.text: Keep far from a false charge, and do not kill the innocent or the righteous, for I will not justify the guilty.

lines.text: Every good Bible student should notice the tension: God says He will not justify the guilty, and Paul says He justifies the ungodly. All are wicked (3:10-18), and the Law brings wrath (4:15).

God's justice is upheld because He does not ignore sin: He acquits the wicked because the righteousness of Christ, 'delivered over on account of our transgressions,' is applied to them by faith (Romans 4:25).
Study note (added): Proverbs 17:15 calls justifying the wicked an abomination. That is the problem the cross answers (Romans 3:26).

left.text: “Blessed are those whose lawless deeds have been forgiven, / And whose sins have been covered. / “Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will not take into account.”

right.text: How blessed is the man whose iniquity Yahweh will not take into account, / And in whose spirit there is no deceit!

lines.text: A second witness: David, the king, speaks of 'the blessing on the man to whom God counts righteousness apart from works' (Romans 4:6). Counting righteousness and not counting sin are two sides of one gift.

left.text: How then was it counted? While he was circumcised, or uncircumcised? Not while circumcised, but while uncircumcised; and he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had while uncircumcised, so that he might be the father of all who believe without being circumcised, that righteousness might be counted to them,

right.text: And you shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be the sign of the covenant between Me and you.

lines.text: Genesis 15 (faith counted) comes before Genesis 17 (circumcision). The teacher calls this the crucial fact that paves the way for Gentiles to be sons and daughters of Abraham.
Abraham himself came from Ur of the Chaldeans (Genesis 11:31): a man from the nations, counted righteous by faith.

SEAL.title: God alone walked between the pieces

left.text: Now it happened that the sun had set, and it was very dark, and behold, there appeared a smoking oven and a flaming torch which passed between these pieces. On that day Yahweh cut a covenant with Abram, saying, “To your seed I have given this land, / From the river of Egypt as far as the great river, the river Euphrates:

right.text: For this reason it is by faith, in order that it may be according to grace, so that the promise will be guaranteed to all the seed, not only to those who are of the Law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all—

lines.text: Abraham presents the animals, but 'a deep sleep fell upon Abram' (Genesis 15:12) and God alone passes between the pieces. The covenant is grounded entirely in God's initiative, character and faithfulness.
That is Paul's point: Abraham's faith is real and responsive, but God's faithfulness comes first and makes the promise certain.

left.text: For the promise to Abraham or to his seed that he would be heir of the world was not through the Law, but through the righteousness of faith.

right.text: And I will bless those who bless you,And the one who curses you I will curse.And in you all the families of the earth will be blessed.”

lines.text: The teacher finds the 'heir of the world' promise in Genesis 12:3 and in Genesis 13:16, 'I will make your seed as the dust of the earth.' Romans 4:13-16 retraces 1:17: God's faithful character guarantees the promise, and Abraham receives it by faithful trust.
'For the Law brings about wrath' (Romans 4:15). If the promise depended on Law-keeping, it would fail.

left.text: as it is written, “A father of many nations have I made you”—in the presence of Him whom he believed, even God, who gives life to the dead and calls into being that which does not exist.

right.text: And no longer shall your name be called Abram, / But your name shall be Abraham; / For I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.

lines.text: The pattern of God's promise and Abraham's trusting response repeats through 4:17, 18, 20, 21, 24 and 25.

left.text: And without becoming weak in faith he contemplated his own body, now as good as dead since he was about a hundred years old, and the deadness of Sarah’s womb; yet, with respect to the promise of God, he did not waver in unbelief but grew strong in faith, giving glory to God, and being fully assured that what God had promised, He was able also to do.

right.text: Is anything too difficult for Yahweh? At the appointed time I will return to you, at this time next year, and Sarah will have a son.”

lines.text: The son of promise came through Abraham's 'dead' body and Sarah's barren womb. 'What a picture,' says the teacher.
Study note (added): Hebrews 11:11-12 gives Sarah's side: she 'regarded Him faithful who had promised.'

left.text: but for our sake also, to whom it will be counted, as those who believe upon Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead, He who was delivered over on account of our transgressions, and was raised on account of our justification.

right.text: As a result of the anguish of His soul, / He will see it and be satisfied; / By His knowledge the Righteous One, / My Servant, will justify the many, / As He will bear their iniquities.

lines.text: God also brings life to the dead through Jesus Christ. 'Delivered up for our sins' comes from Isaiah 53, where the Righteous One makes many righteous and bears their iniquities: God's righteousness again.

BACKGROUND.p: In Genesis 15 Abram cuts animals in two, and 'a smoking oven and a flaming torch' pass between the pieces (15:17). Jeremiah 34:18 describes the same rite: those who passed between the halves of a calf called a curse on themselves if they broke the covenant. Only God passes through in Genesis 15.

Later Jewish writings praised Abraham as faithful in testing (for example 1 Maccabees 2:52, which quotes Genesis 15:6 after the binding of Isaac). Paul stresses the order in Genesis: faith counted (chapter 15) before circumcision (chapter 17) and before the testing (chapter 22).
Ur is usually identified with Tell el-Muqayyar in southern Iraq, excavated by Leonard Woolley in the 1920s-30s. Joshua 24:2 says Abraham's fathers 'served other gods' beyond the River.

James 2:21-23 also quotes Genesis 15:6, pointing to Abraham's works in Genesis 22 as the faith that was 'fulfilled.' Paul answers boasting in works of the Law; James answers faith without deeds. Both use the same verse.

DEBATES.p: The video reads righteousness in Romans 4 as covenant belonging or fellowship, close to scholars who stress covenant membership. Reformation readings stress an imputed righteous standing before God's court. The video holds both: covenant bond, and Christ's righteousness applied by faith.

Some read 'faith is counted as righteousness' to mean God accepts faith in place of righteousness; others say faith is the instrument that receives Christ's righteousness. The video: faith is the open basin, not a matching contribution.

DEBATES.h: Faith versus works: Paul and James
DEBATES.p: Both cite Genesis 15:6. Most interpreters see them answering different errors rather than contradicting each other; how to fit them together is discussed by every tradition.

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: The video cites Genesis 15:12 for God passing between the pieces. Verse 12 is the deep sleep; the smoking oven and flaming torch pass between the pieces in Genesis 15:17.
The video reads Isaiah 53:11 as 'make many to be accounted righteous'; the LSB reads 'will justify the many.'
'Eight times' checks out in the LSB: 'righteousness' appears in 4:3, 5, 6, 9, 11 (twice), 13 and 22. The video's read-through lists seven verses because 4:11 has it twice.
Calling Abraham 'a Gentile' is a useful shorthand (he was from Ur, before Israel existed), but the category Jew and Gentile came later.

QUESTIONS: Why does it matter that Abraham was counted righteous before circumcision?
How do you hold together 'I will not justify the guilty' and 'Him who justifies the ungodly'?
What does God passing alone between the pieces tell you about His promises?
Does 'covenant belonging' help you read Romans 4? Where might it fall short?
Where do you act as if you fill your own plunge pool?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: Picture a cascading waterfall. Water barrels over the edge into tiered plunge pools; each pool fills only because water pours down from above, and then it overflows into the next. God's covenant faithfulness is the waterfall itself, initiating, sustaining and pouring out. Our faith is not a matching contribution; it is the open basin that receives what He gives and lets it overflow. The overflow is not the basis of righteousness; God is. The teacher admits he sometimes acts as if he fills his own pool. Psalm 37:5-6 says the Lord 'will bring forth your righteousness as the light,' and Philippians 3:9 speaks of 'the righteousness which is from God upon faith.' He calls himself a former 'obnoxious, self-centered, egotistical atheist' whom God crushed in order to save and change. 'I didn't do that.'
APPLICATION_ADDED: Study note (added): write Romans 4:20-21 on a card. Next to it, list one promise of God you find hard to believe right now, and pray it back to Him daily this week.

## Summary (from the video)
- The teacher reads Romans 4:1-25. Abraham 'believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness' (4:3). To the one who does not work but believes in Him who justifies the ungodly, faith is counted as righteousness, as David also says (4:4-8). Abraham was counted righteous before he was circumcised, so he is the father of all who believe (4:9-12). The promise came through the righteousness of faith, not the Law (4:13-16). Abraham believed God, who gives life to the dead, and it was written for our sake too: Jesus 'was delivered over on account of our transgressions, and was raised on account of our justification' (4:17-25).
- Recap: Romans 1:17 explains 1:16. The righteousness of God is revealed out of God's covenant faithfulness into the faithful response of the believer. Romans 4 replays that pattern through Abraham, again and again (4:17, 18, 20, 21, 24, 25).
- Abraham came from Ur (Genesis 11) and was counted righteous before circumcision (Genesis 15:6; 17:10-14). That paves the way for Gentiles to be his sons and daughters. In Genesis 15, a deep sleep fell on Abraham and God alone passed between the pieces: the covenant rests entirely on God's faithfulness.
- Romans 4:5 is shocking: God 'justifies the ungodly,' yet Exodus 23:7 says 'I will not justify the guilty.' Everyone is wicked (3:10-18) and the Law brings wrath (4:15). God acquits the wicked not by ignoring sin but because the righteousness of Christ is applied to them by faith. Other connections: Psalm 32:1-2; Genesis 12:3; 13:16; 17:5; Isaiah 53:11.
- Paul uses 'righteousness' eight times in Romans 4. The teacher suggests reading it as 'covenant belonging' and walks through 4:3, 5, 6, 9, 11, 13 and 22 that way. Paul has rubbed the Old Testament into his words like a dry rub on meat on the grill.
- The lesson: 'Righteousness is the covenant bond God forms and believers step into by faith.' Marriage pictures it: God's promise keeping and our promise trusting. The application is a cascading waterfall filling plunge pools: God is the source, and our faith is the open basin that receives and overflows (Psalm 37:4-6; Philippians 3:9).

## Before circumcision, by promise
1. Romans 4:9-12; Genesis 17:10-11: Before he was circumcised
   Paul (Romans 4:10-11, LSB): "How then was it counted? While he was circumcised, or uncircumcised? Not while circumcised, but while uncircumcised; and he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had while uncircumcised, so that he might be the father of all who believe without being circumcised, that righteousness might be counted to them,"
   Genesis (Genesis 17:11, LSB): "And you shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be the sign of the covenant between Me and you."
   (video) Genesis 15 (faith counted) comes before Genesis 17 (circumcision). The teacher calls this the crucial fact that paves the way for Gentiles to be sons and daughters of Abraham.
   (video) Abraham himself came from Ur of the Chaldeans (Genesis 11:31): a man from the nations, counted righteous by faith. (Genesis 11:31)
2. Genesis 15:12, 17; Romans 4:16: God alone walked between the pieces
   Genesis (Genesis 15:17-18, LSB): "Now it happened that the sun had set, and it was very dark, and behold, there appeared a smoking oven and a flaming torch which passed between these pieces. On that day Yahweh cut a covenant with Abram, saying, “To your seed I have given this land, / From the river of Egypt as far as the great river, the river Euphrates:"
   Paul (Romans 4:16, LSB): "For this reason it is by faith, in order that it may be according to grace, so that the promise will be guaranteed to all the seed, not only to those who are of the Law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all—"
   (video) Abraham presents the animals, but 'a deep sleep fell upon Abram' (Genesis 15:12) and God alone passes between the pieces. The covenant is grounded entirely in God's initiative, character and faithfulness. (Genesis 15:12)
   (video) That is Paul's point: Abraham's faith is real and responsive, but God's faithfulness comes first and makes the promise certain.
3. Romans 4:13-15; Genesis 12:3: Heir of the world
   Paul (Romans 4:13, LSB): "For the promise to Abraham or to his seed that he would be heir of the world was not through the Law, but through the righteousness of faith."
   Yahweh to Abram (Genesis 12:3, LSB): "And I will bless those who bless you,And the one who curses you I will curse.And in you all the families of the earth will be blessed.”"
   (video) The teacher finds the 'heir of the world' promise in Genesis 12:3 and in Genesis 13:16, 'I will make your seed as the dust of the earth.' Romans 4:13-16 retraces 1:17: God's faithful character guarantees the promise, and Abraham receives it by faithful trust. (Genesis 13:16; Romans 1:17)
   (video) 'For the Law brings about wrath' (Romans 4:15). If the promise depended on Law-keeping, it would fail.

## God who gives life to the dead
1. Romans 4:17-18; Genesis 17:5: A father of many nations
   Paul (Romans 4:17, LSB): "as it is written, “A father of many nations have I made you”—in the presence of Him whom he believed, even God, who gives life to the dead and calls into being that which does not exist."
   Yahweh to Abram (Genesis 17:5, LSB): "And no longer shall your name be called Abram, / But your name shall be Abraham; / For I have made you the father of a multitude of nations."
   (video) The pattern of God's promise and Abraham's trusting response repeats through 4:17, 18, 20, 21, 24 and 25.
2. Romans 4:19-21; Genesis 18:11-14: As good as dead
   Paul (Romans 4:19-21, LSB): "And without becoming weak in faith he contemplated his own body, now as good as dead since he was about a hundred years old, and the deadness of Sarah’s womb; yet, with respect to the promise of God, he did not waver in unbelief but grew strong in faith, giving glory to God, and being fully assured that what God had promised, He was able also to do."
   Yahweh (Genesis 18:14, LSB): "Is anything too difficult for Yahweh? At the appointed time I will return to you, at this time next year, and Sarah will have a son.”"
   (video) The son of promise came through Abraham's 'dead' body and Sarah's barren womb. 'What a picture,' says the teacher.
   [Background] Study note (added): Hebrews 11:11-12 gives Sarah's side: she 'regarded Him faithful who had promised.' (Hebrews 11:11-12)
3. Romans 4:23-25; Isaiah 53:11: Raised for our justification
   Paul (Romans 4:24-25, LSB): "but for our sake also, to whom it will be counted, as those who believe upon Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead, He who was delivered over on account of our transgressions, and was raised on account of our justification."
   Isaiah (Isaiah 53:11, LSB): "As a result of the anguish of His soul, / He will see it and be satisfied; / By His knowledge the Righteous One, / My Servant, will justify the many, / As He will bear their iniquities."
   (video) God also brings life to the dead through Jesus Christ. 'Delivered up for our sins' comes from Isaiah 53, where the Righteous One makes many righteous and bears their iniquities: God's righteousness again.

## Key people
- Abraham: Counted righteous by faith before circumcision; the father of all who believe, Jew and Gentile. [Background] From Ur of the Chaldeans via Haran (Genesis 11:31); Joshua 24:2 says his fathers 'served other gods.'
- Sarah: Her barren womb, like Abraham's 'dead' body, shows God gives life to the dead. [Background] She laughed at the promise (Genesis 18:12) and bore Isaac at the appointed time.
- David: Psalm 32:1-2: the blessing of forgiven sin, quoted in 4:7-8. [Background] Psalm 32 is headed 'Of David. A Maskil.'
- The Servant (Isaiah 53): The Righteous One who will justify the many; behind 'delivered over' in 4:25. [Background] The New Testament identifies the Servant with Jesus (Acts 8:32-35).
- Paul: An ex-Pharisee whose words are 'flavored' with the Old Testament like a dry rub. [Background] He makes the same Abraham argument in Galatians 3:6-9.

## Places [Background]
- Ur (named in the video): Abraham's starting point: 'Ur of the Chaldeans' (Genesis 11:31).
- Haran: Where Terah's family settled on the way to Canaan (Genesis 11:31).
- Shechem: Abram's first altar in the land (Genesis 12:6-7).
- Hebron: Abraham settled by the oaks of Mamre (Genesis 13:18), where the promise of Isaac came (Genesis 18).

## Key terms
- Counted (credited): Reckoned to someone's account; the key verb of Romans 4 (4:3, 4, 5, 6, 9, 11, 22).
- Righteousness: Right standing with God. The video's paraphrase: 'covenant belonging,' the bond God forms and believers step into by faith.
- Justifies the ungodly: God declares the ungodly righteous on the basis of faith (Romans 4:5).
- Seal: A mark that confirms and authenticates; circumcision sealed the righteousness Abraham already had by faith (Romans 4:11).
- Heir of the world: Abraham's promised inheritance, widened from the land to the world (Romans 4:13).
- Cutting a covenant: A covenant ratified by passing between halves of sacrificed animals (Genesis 15:9-18; compare Jeremiah 34:18). [Background]
- Covenant faithfulness: God's reliability to keep His promises; the video's key to 1:17 and Romans 4.

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- Walking between the pieces: In Genesis 15 Abram cuts animals in two, and 'a smoking oven and a flaming torch' pass between the pieces (15:17). Jeremiah 34:18 describes the same rite: those who passed between the halves of a calf called a curse on themselves if they broke the covenant. Only God passes through in Genesis 15.
- Abraham in Jewish tradition: Later Jewish writings praised Abraham as faithful in testing (for example 1 Maccabees 2:52, which quotes Genesis 15:6 after the binding of Isaac). Paul stresses the order in Genesis: faith counted (chapter 15) before circumcision (chapter 17) and before the testing (chapter 22).
- Ur of the Chaldeans: Ur is usually identified with Tell el-Muqayyar in southern Iraq, excavated by Leonard Woolley in the 1920s-30s. Joshua 24:2 says Abraham's fathers 'served other gods' beyond the River.
- Paul and James on Abraham: James 2:21-23 also quotes Genesis 15:6, pointing to Abraham's works in Genesis 22 as the faith that was 'fulfilled.' Paul answers boasting in works of the Law; James answers faith without deeds. Both use the same verse.

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- Righteousness as 'covenant belonging'? The video reads righteousness in Romans 4 as covenant belonging or fellowship, close to scholars who stress covenant membership. Reformation readings stress an imputed righteous standing before God's court. The video holds both: covenant bond, and Christ's righteousness applied by faith.
- Is faith itself the righteousness? Some read 'faith is counted as righteousness' to mean God accepts faith in place of righteousness; others say faith is the instrument that receives Christ's righteousness. The video: faith is the open basin, not a matching contribution.
- Faith versus works: Paul and James Both cite Genesis 15:6. Most interpreters see them answering different errors rather than contradicting each other; how to fit them together is discussed by every tradition.

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- The video cites Genesis 15:12 for God passing between the pieces. Verse 12 is the deep sleep; the smoking oven and flaming torch pass between the pieces in Genesis 15:17.
- The video reads Isaiah 53:11 as 'make many to be accounted righteous'; the LSB reads 'will justify the many.'
- 'Eight times' checks out in the LSB: 'righteousness' appears in 4:3, 5, 6, 9, 11 (twice), 13 and 22. The video's read-through lists seven verses because 4:11 has it twice.
- Calling Abraham 'a Gentile' is a useful shorthand (he was from Ur, before Israel existed), but the category Jew and Gentile came later.

## Reflection and discussion questions
1. Why does it matter that Abraham was counted righteous before circumcision?
2. How do you hold together 'I will not justify the guilty' and 'Him who justifies the ungodly'?
3. What does God passing alone between the pieces tell you about His promises?
4. Does 'covenant belonging' help you read Romans 4? Where might it fall short?
5. Where do you act as if you fill your own plunge pool?

## Application
- (video) Picture a cascading waterfall. Water barrels over the edge into tiered plunge pools; each pool fills only because water pours down from above, and then it overflows into the next. God's covenant faithfulness is the waterfall itself, initiating, sustaining and pouring out. Our faith is not a matching contribution; it is the open basin that receives what He gives and lets it overflow. The overflow is not the basis of righteousness; God is. The teacher admits he sometimes acts as if he fills his own pool. Psalm 37:5-6 says the Lord 'will bring forth your righteousness as the light,' and Philippians 3:9 speaks of 'the righteousness which is from God upon faith.' He calls himself a former 'obnoxious, self-centered, egotistical atheist' whom God crushed in order to save and change. 'I didn't do that.'
- Study note (added): write Romans 4:20-21 on a card. Next to it, list one promise of God you find hard to believe right now, and pray it back to Him daily this week.
